headline: Medtronic grows 6.5% organically as cardiac ablation surges 58%, but only reiterates its full-year outlook
takeaway: Revenue rose 4.5% to $9.36 billion, or 6.5% organically, with cardiac ablation up 58%. Adjusted EPS was $1.34 and the full-year guidance of 7.25–7.75% organic growth and $5.94–6.00 EPS was kept unchanged. The shares fell 4.6% on the day.
results: Revenue was $9.364 billion, up 4.5% reported and 6.5% organically. This is the first quarter after the MiniMed diabetes business was split off on October 15, so the reported figure carries less diabetes revenue than a year ago. GAAP earnings per share were $2.20, lifted by items tied to the separation; adjusted EPS was $1.34.

Cardiovascular was the engine: revenue of $3.785 billion grew 10.4% organically, and Cardiac Ablation Solutions grew 58%, with the United States up about 80%. Neuroscience grew 3.2% organically to $2.705 billion and Medical Surgical 4.4% to $2.245 billion. Medtronic also announced its intent to acquire Contego Medical, a maker of carotid and peripheral vascular devices.
mgmt: Chairman and chief executive Geoff Martha called it a strong quarter with broad-based performance and said execution gives him confidence in sustaining the momentum. Chief financial officer Thierry Piéton said the company is investing behind its highest-priority growth opportunities while keeping a disciplined focus on costs.

Management reiterated its fiscal 2027 outlook: organic revenue growth of 7.25% to 7.75% and adjusted earnings per share of $5.94 to $6.00. It said it is maintaining these ranges while absorbing the impact of the diabetes separation, and did not raise either number despite the strength in cardiovascular. The quarter also brought reimbursement codes for the Symplicity Spyral renal denervation system from January 2028 and new FDA clearances for the Hugo surgical robot.
view: The growth story at Medtronic has narrowed to one product line. Cardiac ablation growing close to 60% is exceptional, but neuroscience and surgical, which together are larger than cardiovascular, are growing at 3–4%. The group’s organic rate is respectable for a company of this size, yet it depends heavily on a single franchise keeping its pace against Boston Scientific and Johnson & Johnson.

The 4.6% drop on the day, to $96.13, suggests investors had hoped the ablation surge would translate into a higher full-year forecast. Keeping the guide unchanged after a strong quarter implies a softer second half, or that management is leaving room for the dilution from the diabetes split and the cost of new launches.

At about 16 times the midpoint of this year’s EPS guidance, Medtronic is priced as a slow grower with a reliable dividend. That is fair if the rest of the portfolio stays at low single digits. The upside case needs ablation to keep compounding and the renal denervation and robotic surgery launches to add a second leg; until one of those shows up in the numbers, the valuation is unlikely to expand much.
watch: Whether cardiac ablation keeps growing above 40% as competitors launch new catheters, early revenue from renal denervation and the Hugo surgical robot, and whether the full-year outlook is raised in February.
